claims.statement: A deterministic seeded bounded search over 30 order-91/order-243 root multi-hub tree recipes tested all 582 eligible tree/rank rows and found no positive full ordinary favorable-leaf aggregate; the two anchor trees reproduce their positive marked terms alongside negative complete sums.
claims.scope: Finite computation on the 30 generated recipes and all eligible p values for each recipe as specified in C1-F1 REPORT.md and evidence/search_families.py. It is not a universal result over ordinary trees.
claims.reason: retained — The bounded result replays exactly from scratch-local copies: the full source and replay JSON objects agree, with 30 candidates, 582 eligible rows (137 at order 91 and 445 at order 243), and zero positive aggregates. The graph construction, forest polynomial recurrence, terminal-rank first-descent check, strict eligibility range, strict leaf selector, rank shift, original support/neighborhood operations, and distinct same-support leaf summation are consistent with the stated calculation. Both standing controls reproduce their exact positive marked terms and negative full sums, supporting the stated finite observation while demonstrating that local positivity does not refute an aggregate. The result remains bounded to the seeded sample and supplies no universal proof or counterexample.

limitations: The seeded recipes are not exhaustive over multi-hub trees or ordinary trees, so the finite nonpositive sums do not establish the universal assertion.
Replay uses the same pinned dynamic-programming evaluator in a local copy; this establishes reproducibility and source-output consistency, not independent algorithmic validation.
